title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement best separates a workflow from an agent when both use a language model and tools?

options.text: A workflow calls the model once, while an agent calls the model many times
A workflow's steps are set by code, while an agent's model chooses its steps
A workflow cannot use any tools, while an agent is the only one that can
A workflow needs a person to approve steps, while an agent runs by itself

items.stem: A student's message reaches this Python code: it always calls check_calendar(machine, date), then always calls the model once with the calendar result to write a reply, then returns the reply. The model never chooses which tool runs or whether to run another. What is this system?

options.text: An agent, because it calls a tool and the model uses the result
An agent, because the model writes the final reply to the student
Neither, because a system with only one tool is too small to count
A workflow, because the code fixes the steps and their order in advance

items.stem: In one sentence: in an agent, what decides which step comes next, and in a fixed workflow, what decides it?

Your team must handle one makerspace task: every incoming booking request goes through the same three steps (extract machine and time, check the calendar, write a confirmation). Money for model usage is tight. Which design is the better choice?

options.text: A fixed workflow, because the steps are known and an agent would add cost
An agent, because any task with tools should let the model plan the steps
An agent, because it is cheaper per request when a task has several steps
A fixed workflow, because it adapts better when the steps differ each time

items.stem: Assume every model call costs the same. A fixed workflow makes exactly 2 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 6 model calls per request, because it loops. Over 500 requests, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow?
In one or two sentences: what is a property of a task that would justify using an agent instead of a fixed workflow?
